# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible rival I found is:

> **Mirror only width-3 inputs; for every other width, horizontally duplicate the input.**

Formally, for a grid `g`, use the intended `hconcat(g, flip_lr(g))` when
`width(g) == 3`; otherwise use `hconcat(g, g)`. All four canonical
demonstrations have width 3, so this rival matches every demonstration exactly.
It is stronger than plain duplication because it deliberately agrees on the
entire observed canonical support while differing off that support.

## Exact disagreement

Input:

```json
[
  [1, 2, 3, 4],
  [4, 3, 2, 1],
  [1, 1, 2, 3]
]
```

The intended rule returns:

```json
[
  [1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3, 2, 1],
  [4, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4],
  [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1]
]
```

The width-gated rival takes its non-width-3 branch and returns:

```json
[
  [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4],
  [4, 3, 2, 1, 4, 3, 2, 1],
  [1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 2, 3]
]
```

## How I checked it

I executed the canonical Racket authority with the included offline bridge. The
receipt is `checks/question-shortcut/racket.json`; it records executed rule hash
`1bf14d2f29b0`, final generator SHA-256
`2cba4e98ff256db67b2af11eba2e71c915badbc042c8b0e56040488445625314`,
and output SHA-256
`5a7a209d825a32a9f459e78dc9affd43ce693e149b414a956e85b26aea1eacf5`.
The rival output is independently retained in
`checks/question-shortcut/rival-output.json`.

## Does the generator emit disagreement cases?

Yes. With final source bytes, `seed=0`, `sample_index=1`,
`difficulty="easy"`, and no overrides emits this left-right-asymmetric 3×5 input:

```json
[
  [3, 3, 3, 1, 3],
  [1, 3, 3, 4, 1],
  [3, 1, 3, 8, 3]
]
```

Because its width is 5, the rival duplicates it while the intended rule mirrors
it, so their outputs differ. The source-bound recipe is
`checks/question-shortcut/generated-witness.json`; the same case is retained and
replayed under
`repo/generators/19158f03ecb2/counterexamples/review-a1e69e9fdec20d2f.json`.
